holidays.name: National Cotton Candy Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the fluffy, sugary cloud of spun sugar that has delighted fairgoers for generations. Grab a cone and let your teeth regret everything.
holidays.origin: Cotton candy was introduced to a wide audience at the 1904 St. Louis World's Fair, created by dentist William Morrison and confectioner John C. Wharton. National Cotton Candy Day was established in the United States as a food observance in the 2000s.
holidays.funFact: The machine that made cotton candy was co-invented by a dentist, and the pair sold about 68,000 boxes of the treat at the 1904 World's Fair.

holidays.name: International Civil Aviation Day
holidays.description: A United Nations observance celebrating the airplanes, pilots, air traffic controllers, and systems that make worldwide flight possible, so you can complain about legroom at 35,000 feet.
holidays.origin: It was first observed in 1994 to mark the 50th anniversary of the signing of the Convention on International Civil Aviation in Chicago on December 7, 1944, which created the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO).
holidays.funFact: The Chicago Convention of 1944 was signed while World War II was still raging, yet it laid down the rules for peacetime global air travel.

holidays.name: Letter Writing Day
holidays.description: A day to put down your phone, pick up a pen, and send an actual handwritten letter to someone. Stamps are the original push notification.
holidays.origin: Letter Writing Day is an informal, unofficial observance that grew from the popularity of national days promoting handwritten correspondence, and it is often celebrated in early December as people prepare holiday cards.
holidays.funFact: The Pony Express carried letters across the American West in about 10 days, and it only operated for roughly 18 months in 1860 and 1861.

holidays.name: Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day
holidays.description: Not quirky, but a solemn observance worth noting, as this date is remembered for the 1941 attack on Pearl Harbor. Flags are flown at half-staff in honor of those who died.
holidays.origin: Congress designated December 7 as National Pearl Harbor Remembrance Day in 1994 to honor the more than 2,400 Americans who lost their lives in the 1941 attack.
holidays.funFact: The USS Arizona Memorial still leaks small amounts of oil from the sunken ship, which are known as the 'black tears of the Arizona.'

holidays.name: Santa's Reindeer Appreciation Day Adjacent: Tamale Season Kickoff
holidays.description: In many Latino communities, early December marks the start of tamale-making season, when families gather in assembly lines to spread masa, add fillings, and wrap dozens of corn husk bundles for the holidays.
holidays.origin: Tamales have been made in Mesoamerica for thousands of years, and the tradition of making them for Christmas and Las Posadas gatherings grew from Mexican and Central American cultures.
holidays.funFact: Tamales date back as far as 8000 to 5000 BCE, and Aztec and Maya warriors reportedly carried them as portable food.
